subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment mode clarifications + benchmark request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment mode clarifications + benchmark request

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and two asks so we can converge on a pilot path:

Recap (what we heard)
- Target p95 latency for user-facing scoring: ~50–80 ms (depending on model and sequence length)
- Peak QPS: ~1,100 sustained during end-of-day batch windows; average QPS ~220
- Payloads: avg prompt length ~260 tokens, 95th percentile ~800 tokens (longer for batch jobs)
- Data residency: US only for now; potential VPC requirement for Prod if we move to private deployment later

Our initial recommendation (based on those numbers):
- Start with Hosted API for the pilot to move fast and collect real traffic patterns. Hosted supports the model variants we demoed and will let you iterate on prompts and routing without infra commits.
- If sustained peak QPS > ~800 with tight p95 targets across all users, we typically recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) for predictable throughput + isolation.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you send a 48–72 hour representative traffic extract (CSV). Key columns: timestamp, endpoint, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, success/fail flag. We attached a sample CSV template (fastfin_qps_profile.csv) — you can paste a snippet or export.
2) Are you able to run a small benchmark test window next week? If yes, we can provide a non-prod API key and a short-run load script; we’ll capture p50/p95/p99 and CSV-level token billing estimates.
3) Please confirm whether a Reserved / Procurement conversation would be possible in parallel if the pilot shows predictable utilization.

Attachments: fastfin_qps_profile.csv (template), redwood_quick_pilot_plan.pdf (pilot timeline + roles)

If it helps, Marissa and Naomi are cc’d to coordinate scheduling and the benchmark. I can also route a quick PSA (SLA and cost tradeoffs one-pager) if your procurement team will want it.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0147

From: Elena Morales <elena@fastfin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, ops@fastfin.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment mode clarifications + benchmark request

Thanks Ben —

Appreciate the crisp recap. A few quick notes:
- The QPS numbers are accurate for our production traffic spike; the 1,100 is a conservative estimate for the EOD batch but could spike to ~1,300 during promotions.
- We can extract a 72-hour sample. Ops will review formatting.
- Procurement: yes we’ll need a parallel pricing ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted (monthly committed vs pay-as-you-go) — can Marissa share an initial estimate?

Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, FastFin
elena@fastfin.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment mode clarifications + benchmark request

Elena —

Thanks for the quick response. I’ll pull a Hosted vs Dedicated ballpark for the numbers Ben listed (I’ll include committed pricing bands and an example breakeven calc for a 6- and 12-month commit). Expect that by EOD Friday.

On the benchmark: we can provision a temporary non-prod API key and a load script that simulates your token distribution (we’ll align on concurrency and stage). Two logistical asks before we run:
- Can you share a small sample test corpus (10–20 representative prompts) so we use realistic sequences and response lengths?
- Do you have any internal throughput guardrails (e.g., maximum concurrent connections from a single IP) we should be aware of?

I’ll also add a brief note on what metrics we’ll capture in the benchmark results (p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, token-unit cost estimate, and a suggested deployment recommendation).

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Morales <elena@fastfin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment mode clarifications + benchmark request

Marissa —

We can do the test corpus and the 72-hour extract. Ops will send the CSV by tomorrow; test corpus attached inline below. No unusual connection guardrails — we throttle via an internal queue but can open a short window for load testing.

Test prompts (10 samples):
1) "Resolve customer dispute for card transaction ID 89234 — summarize probable cause"
2) "Generate 3 policy-compliant response templates for chargeback dispute"
3) "Given transaction log snippet (20 lines), extract anomalous merchant patterns"
4) "Summarize terms-of-service differences between v2 and v3 of our payment API"
5) "Draft a short customer notification for scheduled maintenance affecting ACH"
6) "Rewrite the following KB article for product managers: <snip>"
7) "Produce 20 training examples for fraud classifier labeling"
8) "Batch-score these 500 customer messages for sentiment"
9) "Compress and normalize transaction descriptions for downstream aggregation"
10) "Translate a Spanish support reply to English preserving tone and policy constraints"

We’ll send the CSV and a short note on the traffic window. Looking forward to the benchmark.

—Elena
